rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Banned words — grep zero-tolerance.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 5: 'This is crucially the step that changes how the run behaves.' — body grep for the banned set returns 1 hit (derive-body-view.js banned_words, planted_proof true, body_hits 1). Harm the rule prevents: consultancy/lab register that flinches an engineer reader; present here, the adverb is doing no work the sentence needs.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Cut 'crucially'; the sentence states the claim without it.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Ritual / ceremony — hard ban in any curriculum/training surface.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 11: 'Treat this as a ritual you repeat at the start of every session.' — ritual_ceremony grep body_hits 1 (planted_proof true). Harm: the word reframes the exercise as ceremony, which is exactly the Scrum-retro register the curriculum exists to replace. Present.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Word is 'exercise' (or 'move'/'step'): 'Run this at the start of every session.'

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No stale markers, no fixed retrospectives, no session biography.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 49: 'This section previously said something different; it was fixed on 2026-01-14.' — session_biography grep body_hits 1 ('previously') and dated_line body_hits 1, both in body region (lines 1-65), no fence, no accept-note. Verb states a transition, so the tense test fires as well as the grep. Harm: changelog in a student-facing body; the student loses nothing if it vanishes.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Delete the sentence outright; history is git.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Register match.

Peer voice does not reassure a professional that skipping is allowed. Non-blocking: register nuance, not a hard grep.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Cut the sentence; the optional framing is already carried by 'Push back on the five.'

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't smuggle terms of art from maintainer into body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Verbatim-frame-cite in reference artefact.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Authoring-process rule about capturing a maintainer's verbal frame into a reference artefact; no reference artefact is being authored here.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cap practitioner attribution at one student-side mention per module.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No practitioner is named anywhere in the body region (lines 1-65); the roster names sit in the backing block only.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Punchy framing keeps punch; carve-out lives downstream.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 55-58: '## Anything can be reverse-engineered' is followed by exactly two bullets (`sed -n '55,59p' ... | grep -c '^- '` returns 2), and neither names a boundary. The file's own stance block (134) asserts the boundary 'carries its boundary in the third bullet per check_writing.md 12' and tells judges to 'read the third bullet before flagging' — that bullet does not exist. Harm: a superlative slogan shipped with no carve-out, which is the exact configuration 12 exists to prevent, and the maintainer believes it is covered.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Restore the boundary bullet (extraction quality tracks the quality of the artifact sampled) or correct the stance note; do not soften the header.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Value-prop / positioning framing belongs in sales copy + project strategy docs, NOT student-facing curriculum body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: 43 'it pays back on every session after this one.' — a payoff claim about the student's own sessions, not a positioning move; no 'vendor', no 'not aspirational', no marketing-vs-practitioner frame anywhere in lines 1-65.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Watch out for planting jargon too early.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: 57 'reverse-engineered with an LLM'. 'LLM' is legal AE101 working vocabulary per 4's commonly-known-LLM-vocabulary clause; 'connector' is accept-noted at L72. No training-architecture term ('send-off', 'the back half') appears in body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Audit closer when trimming body-prose forcing function.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 24: 'At this point the student should notice the test is still red.' — the closer of the first section introduces a definite 'the test' that has no antecedent anywhere in the file, and its claim is contradicted by 62 ('The loop that started with a failing test closed'). Read cold, the reader cannot point at what 'the test' is or what they are told to do. Non-blocking.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Delete with the 7 fix; if a test reference is wanted, anchor it to the upstream fix explicitly.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The **What happened:** block is OPTIONAL — default is to omit it.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 62-64 carries the three moves: count+noun ('Two things came out of one ticket: a close-out note ... and the conventions'), one qualifier ('your team has been encoding in its fields all along'), destination ('The field rules stay in the scrollback'). Past tense throughout, heading is retrospective. Within the 25-40 word band for the first sentence.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No combative verbs about the agent in body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: 39 'Push back on the five.' — push-back is house vocabulary for review pressure on a proposal, not a bark/order/command shape. Verbs directed at the agent elsewhere are 'ask' (33, 45), 'tell' (53), 'have' (7): all peer-flat.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Headers must be literally true about the mechanism.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: 55 '## Anything can be reverse-engineered' — broad, but literally the section's claim and not a spatial metaphor contradicting the mechanism; no 'other X' header presupposing an unnamed primary. Its overreach is filed under 12, not here.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Machine-cadence fat — the shape of good prose without the content.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: 5 'This is ... the step that changes how the run behaves.' — deictic, but 'this' resolves to the exercise the reader just opened, so it is not the empty pointer 19b bans. No empty negation, no bold-label echo, no citation duplication in lines 1-65.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't state a count the adjacent list already holds.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: 33 'propose five bug rules.' — the numeral is the size of an ask sent to the agent, not a tally sitting above a visible list, and 39 ('Push back on the five') reuses it as a handle away from any enumeration. No count sits adjacent to the bullet lists at 28-31 or 57-58.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A slogan that is false as stated is not punchy framing — run the truth test before reaching for 12.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 57 'Anything can be inspected and reverse-engineered with an LLM' is the superlative, and the maintainer has recorded it as a deliberate, contested, L1 stance in the backing block (132-135) rather than an unread claim. Scoped by its own appositive list to inspectable artifacts, so a true reading exists. The defect is the missing boundary bullet, filed under 12.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A claim binds to every body that states it, not just the one holding the stamp.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Cross-file rule; this fire is scoped to one bench fixture with no sibling body in the corpus.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A rule set reconstructed at session start goes stale inside the session — re-derive it per target, not per sweep.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Aspirational destination, never corrective gap.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No narrating student's past or present state.

Harm: patronising descriptive grammar wearing an imperative's hat, on a professional audience. Present. Non-blocking (the blocking half is filed under check_writing 7).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Operational reminders live at moment of use, not only where introduced.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Name the artifact, not the act.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Name the outcome; don't walk a professional through trivial mechanics.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The curriculum does not narrate itself — subject test, then deletion test.

Delete it and 62 closes cleanly. Harm: a cheque the next exercise has to cash, in a recap section that is not on the exempt signposting list. Non-blocking, and worth a maintainer call: it may be deliberately answering where the rules go, in which case it owes an accept-note.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Agents 101 M2+ Debrief — canonical shape.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Agents 101 Debrief shape; no Debrief in this file and the training is AE101.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Trust the prompt over the scaffold.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Three registry prompts carry the whole exercise (22, 35, 47) and no scaffold is shipped; the bug rules and the close-out are produced through the prompts, in the student's own tracker voice.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Mood is a design constraint, not a garnish.
rules_evaluated.evidence: AE101 M1's mood is earned trust, and the beat lands there (17-20, 45). Closest to the module's signature wrong-edit: 11 'Treat this as a ritual you repeat at the start of every session', which pushes toward ceremony register; filed lexically under check_writing 2.

findings.quote: This is crucially the step that changes how the run behaves.
findings.harm: Banned adverb in student-facing body; consultancy/lab register that flinches an engineer reader, and it carries no meaning the sentence loses without it.

findings.quote: Treat this as a ritual you repeat at the start of every session.
findings.harm: Hard-banned word on a curriculum surface; reframes the exercise as ceremony, the exact register the compound loop exists to replace.
findings.fix: 'Run this at the start of every session.' — the word is exercise, move, or step.

findings.quote: At this point the student should notice the test is still red.
findings.harm: Third-person teacher voice in student-facing body, and it reads as delivery mechanics rather than an action the reader can take. The claim is also unanchored ('the test' has no antecedent) and contradicts line 62.
findings.fix: Delete the sentence; if a trainer cue is wanted, it belongs below the maintainer fence.

findings.quote: This section previously said something different; it was fixed on 2026-01-14.
findings.harm: Changelog in a student-facing body: a transition verb plus a bare date, telling the reader about an edit rather than about their work. History is git.

todos.note: 'There is no penalty if you skip this, and it is completely fine either way.' — over-hedge; two named flags in one sentence. Cut it.
Same sentence is the file's clearest register slip against the AE101 quintet: peer voice does not reassure a professional that skipping is allowed.

'## Anything can be reverse-engineered' ships with two bullets and no boundary paragraph, while the backing stance (line 134) tells judges the caveat lives 'in the third bullet'. Restore the boundary bullet or correct the stance note.
'the test is still red' — definite article with no antecedent in the file, and contradicted by line 62. Goes away with the rule-7 deletion.
Same sentence is present-state ascription of what the reader should be perceiving; patronising on a professional audience.
'how the run behaves' — noun-run for the agent's sitting is banned in student-facing body; the word is session.
'The next exercise sweeps this whole session.' — later-beat predicate is cartography; delete and line 62 closes cleanly. If it is deliberately answering where the rules go, it owes an accept-note.
